title: find: search the whole tree
summary: Walk through every folder under a starting point and keep what matches: by name, by type, by size or age.

text: ls shows one folder. find walks into every folder below the start, as deep as it goes.
- First where to start (maze), then the tests that keep what matches.
- Quote the pattern: '*.bak'. Without quotes, the shell may expand it first, with the names of the folder you are in.
A directory can have a name that matches too.
- -type f keeps regular files, -type d directories.
- Tests add up: a path must pass every one of them to be printed.
find prints one path per line, so wc -l counts them.
- find can also act on what it finds (-delete, -exec). Run it once without, to see the list first.
